problem_statement: In NuttX configurations that enable high-resolution timer support, the high-resolution timer API is broken in ordinary tick-based builds. An application that arms an hrtimer and then waits for its expiration callback may wait indefinitely because the callback is never delivered. Cancellation calls such as hrtimer_cancel() and hrtimer_cancel_sync() may also hang or return a negative error status instead of a successful non-negative result. In tickless scheduler configurations, the same high-resolution timer API can fail to operate, and an application that uses it may see the system stop making progress or time out. The required behavior is that, with high-resolution timer support enabled, hrtimer operations must work correctly in both tick-based and tickless builds: armed timers must expire and invoke their callbacks, and hrtimer_cancel() and hrtimer_cancel_sync() must complete and return a non-negative success value. The system must not hang or time out when hrtimer is used in either mode.

superseded_statements.problem_statement: With hrtimer enabled on sim:nsh, the ostest hrtimer test asserts hrtimer_cancel() and hrtimer_cancel_sync() return exactly OK, which fails because these functions return the timer reference count (>= 0) and the previous hrtimer update had restricted hardware timer reprogramming to tickless mode only, breaking hrtimer in tick-based mode. The test must accept any non-negative return (ret >= 0) and require correct hrtimer reprogramming behavior so the suite passes on a tick-based scheduler.

superseded_statements.problem_statement: When the updated OSTest hrtimer test is run in a NuttX configuration that enables hrtimer support, the hrtimer_test case does not complete and ostest times out. The test change in testing/ostest/hrtimer.c updates the checks for hrtimer_cancel and hrtimer_cancel_sync to accept a non-negative return value, but the observed behavior is that the hrtimer test hangs instead of reaching completion and returning status 0. The issue is reproducible with hrtimer enabled and is not confined to tickless operation; it also affects tick-based operation, and tickless operation with hrtimer is not properly supported. The required behavior is that hrtimer functionality works regardless of the scheduler tick mode: hrtimer_cancel and hrtimer_cancel_sync must complete with results accepted by the updated test, the hrtimer_test case must pass, and ostest should terminate normally in both tick-based and tickless configurations.
